title: Security Thinking Before Tools

segments.boardPlan: Write: asset, threat, control, evidence, authorization.
segments.transcript: Cybersecurity starts with responsibility. Before we name a tool, we name what must be protected, what could go wrong, what evidence we have, and what we are authorized to do.

segments.boardPlan: Draw a login page, database, user, attacker, and trust boundary.
segments.transcript: A threat model is a disciplined sketch of reality. We mark assets, actors, entry points, boundaries, threats, mitigations, and assumptions. The drawing keeps us honest.

segments.overlay: Pause and write one asset, one threat, and one authorization boundary for a system you own.
segments.transcript: Pause here. Write one asset, one threat, and one authorization boundary for a system you own. Leave space to revise it.
Good defensive work is careful. We do not test what we do not own or have permission to test, and we do not claim more than evidence supports.

practicePrompts: Draw a threat model for a login page using only safe, hypothetical details.
Write a risk memo that distinguishes evidence from suspicion.
